layers.label: Degenerate core
layers.explanation: An Earth-sized ball of electron-degenerate matter — the whole former star's core, packed to the quantum limit.

layers.label: Planetary nebula
layers.explanation: The red giant's envelope, glowing green-blue as it drifts away — the leftover shell that names the nebula.

hotspots.label: Electron-degenerate interior
hotspots.description: Inside: the core is held open by electrons refusing to be squeezed closer. No fusion — just quantum refusal.

hotspots.label: Planetary nebula (leftover envelope)
hotspots.description: The gas the red giant pushed off, drifting away around the exposed core — the 'planetary' name is a historical accident.

hotspots.label: Dead core — no fusion
hotspots.description: No furnace here. The white glow is leftover heat, radiating away and never re-lit.

hotspots.label: Chandrasekhar limit (1.4 solar masses)
hotspots.description: The ceiling: above ~1.4 solar masses, electron pressure fails and the remnant must become a neutron star or explode.

hotspots.label: Density to the scale of a teaspoon
hotspots.description: A tiny spoon object floats below the dwarf, labelled '5.5 tons' — a visual anchor for the density.

visualStyleNotes: Small marble-white sphere beside a model of Earth at the same scale, warm off-white render, gentle glow. A translucent blue-green shell of drifting gas surrounds the pair. Hotspot beads and labels in the standard umber style — clean, no clutter.
materialNotes: Dwarf: emissive white with soft bloom, slightly blue near the rim. Nebula: faint translucent green-blue fresnel. Earth model: existing blue-and-white globe style from the solar-system scenes, scaled to ~0.55 units.
assetBrief: Procedural Three.js scene: dwarf sphere (radius ~0.5), Earth sphere (radius ~0.55) placed beside it, planetary nebula as a faint translucent ring/cloud, cross-section plane available. Camera frames both bodies; auto-rotate on.
